title: Anthropic IPO Targets $1.4 Trillion Valuation, $64 Billion Raise
summary: Anthropic's IPO targets a $1.4 trillion valuation and up to $64 billion raised. Here's the price range, investor stakes, and what it means for Claude builders.

Anthropic IPO


# Anthropic IPO Targets $1.4 Trillion Valuation, $64 Billion Raise


By OpenTools Team


·


November 11, 2026


Anthropic set a $70 to $78 share price range for its IPO, valuing the Claude maker at roughly $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis. The offering could raise up to $64 billion, with Amazon and Google holding the biggest paper gains. Trading is expected to start November 19 under the ticker ANT.


## The Price: $70 to $78 a Share


[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) set the terms for its initial public offering on Monday. The Claude maker plans to sell shares at $70 to $78 apiece, a range that values the company at up to $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis,[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/anthropic-ipo-raise-much-644-billion-latest-draft-prospectus-shows-2026-11-10/) reported.[AP News](https://apnews.com/article/anthropic-ipo-claude-ai-spacex-openai-amodei-8cf2319c870322019712ab658f71ec55) framed the target at roughly $1.3 trillion, while[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/10/anthropic-sets-ipo-price-range-of-70-to-78-per-share-to-reach-an-implied-valuation-of-1-404-trillion/) calculated a fully diluted valuation of $1.404 trillion at the top of the range. The stock will trade on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, with pricing expected November 18 and first trading November 19.


## A $64 Billion Raise, Plus a $26 Billion Private Placement


The offering is enormous by any measure.[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) is selling 825 million shares, which at the top of the range would raise about $64.4 billion from public investors, according to[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/anthropic-ipo-raise-much-644-billion-latest-draft-prospectus-shows-2026-11-10/) . On top of that, a concurrent private placement will sell $26 billion of non-voting Class N shares to cornerstone investors including Alphabet,[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) , AMD, Broadcom, Micron,[Microsoft](https://opentools.ai/organizations/microsoft) , and TSMC. Combined, the deal could bring in roughly $90 billion.


## Amazon and Google Hold the Biggest Paper Gains


Amazon and[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) ,[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's two largest investors, stand to gain the most. Amazon has put about $18 billion into Anthropic across convertible notes and preferred stock, a position worth roughly $238.7 billion on paper as of September 30, according to[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/what-anthropics-ipo-could-mean-for-amazon-and-google-192716198.html) . Google committed up to $40 billion and held roughly 14% of the company as of early 2025, though that stake has since diluted to about 8% according to PitchBook estimates,[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/27/vcs-will-make-billions-on-anthropics-ipo-but-amazon-is-set-to-make-much-much-more/) reported. The two are also Anthropic's biggest cloud providers: 48% of Anthropic's revenue at the end of 2025 flowed through marketplaces run by Amazon, Google, and[Microsoft](https://opentools.ai/organizations/microsoft) ,[Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/10/26/anthropics-s-1/) noted.


## The Seven Founders Cash Out $250 Million Each


Every one of[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's seven co-founders is selling the same number of shares — 3,378,378 — which would net each of them about $250 million at the midpoint of the range,[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/10/all-7-anthropic-founders-will-each-cash-out-about-250m-in-ipo/) reported. The group, which includes CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei, will keep about 50.1% of voting control after the offering through super-voting Class F shares. Public shareholders get exposure to the AI boom but almost no say in how the company is run.


## Revenue Is Exploding, Losses Are Too


[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's growth is staggering, and so is its spending. Revenue hit $33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up more than 1,200% year over year, with a run-rate of about $81 billion as of October 31,[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/anthropic-ipo-raise-much-644-billion-latest-draft-prospectus-shows-2026-11-10/) reported. The company posted an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of 2026, a figure driven largely by a $72.4 billion non-cash accounting charge tied to its convertible notes,[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/27/-anthropic-ipo-investors-growth-losses-s-1.html) reported. The operating loss was far smaller, and Anthropic generated positive cash from operations for the first time in that same period.


## What the IPO Means for Claude Builders


For developers building on Claude, the IPO is a signal about pricing and stability.[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) has committed roughly $900 billion to future compute, and its own S-1 filing warns that “we do not expect our revenue will[continue](https://opentools.ai/tools/continue) to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all,” as[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/what-anthropics-ipo-could-mean-for-amazon-and-google-192716198.html) quoted. The stakes go beyond one company: if ANT trades well, capital stays cheap for the entire AI ecosystem. If it stumbles, the ripple effects could tighten funding for every startup building on frontier models.
